sections.heading: Can Infrared Technology Detect Roof Leaks? What Infrared Imaging Sees on the Roof Surface

c.v: Infrared technology detects roof leaks indirectly.

runs.v: An infrared camera reads temperature differences on the roof surface, not water: thermal cameras detect temperature differences caused by moisture retention, so thermal imaging detects moisture by identifying temperature anomalies. The sun loads the membrane by day, and after sunset the wet areas stay warmer than the dry areas because saturated insulation carries more thermal mass, which is why infrared inspections are best conducted at night following a sunny day. Infrared scanning provides a comprehensive thermal map of the roof surface, and infrared thermography highlights thermal anomalies indicating moisture in insulation that the human eye cannot see, even when the roofing surface appears intact.

map the extent of water damage under the roofing membrane and can reveal hidden roof leaks before visible damage occurs, so the scan can identify issues before interior damage shows. Early detection of moisture issues helps prevent mold growth and structural decay, and it spares the ceilings and floors below.

c.v: Hot spots are not all leaks.

runs.v: Rooftop equipment, exhaust fans blowing warm air, and recent patches can read warm, so experienced technicians check each anomaly against the roof plan and confirm it before calling it wet. A stain visible to the naked eye on a ceiling can trace to a flashing detail far across the roof, because insulation joints, deck flutes, and the vapor barrier carry it sideways first.

sections.heading: Infrared Thermal Imaging Camera or Moisture Meter: Do Infrared Moisture Meters Work?

c.v: Infrared moisture meters work as screening tools, not as proof.

runs.v: An infrared camera, including the thermal imaging cameras built into some meters, shows surface temperature, while a pin or pinless moisture meter measures moisture at one spot. A leak investigation pairs the two: infrared thermography can be executed rapidly compared with traditional testing methods, so infrared thermal imaging sweeps the whole roof to flag problem areas, and the meter or a core cut confirms each one, the verification ASTM C1153 requires. A pinhole that has not yet wet the insulation needs a different test, electronic leak detection, a method covered by ASTM D7877. A thermal scan added to a home inspection looks at walls and ceilings inside a house; a roof leak investigation starts on the membrane.

sections.heading: Is an Infrared Scan Worth It? Repairs vs. Replacing a Commercial Roof in New Jersey

c.v: An infrared scan is worth it when a flat roof leaks and the owner is weighing repairs against replacing the roof.

runs.v: The infrared roof inspection sizes the wet area before anyone quotes a replacement, so a leak confined to one flashing detail gets a targeted repair, while a saturated field puts replacement on the table. Thermal imaging can identify the areas needing targeted roof repairs, and an infrared survey often prescribes targeted repairs instead of a full roof replacement. Wet insulation has almost zero R-value once saturated, so moisture intrusion can cause significant energy loss and heat loss; infrared scans show where buildings leak energy and help prioritize maintenance to lower utility costs and protect the building. The same ASTM C1153 practice applies from New Jersey to New England.

faqs.q: How does infrared roof leak detection find a leak on an Orange flat roof?

runs.v: It scans the roof after sunset and maps the subsurface wet insulation, which retains solar heat longer than dry insulation and shows as a warm anomaly on the thermal image. Wet insulation carries higher heat capacity and cools more slowly, per Fluke and IIBEC, and ASTM C1153 names this the standard practice for locating wet insulation, per ASTM and the NRCA.

faqs.q: Does infrared imaging find the exact leak entry point?

runs.v: No. Infrared imaging locates the wet insulation, not the leak entry point itself, because the wet area separates from the breach, per Fluke and IIBEC. A Newark Quality Roofing scan traces the verified wet insulation back toward the flashing detail that admits the water.

faqs.q: Why does ASTM C1153 require a core cut on a Valley Arts loft roof?

runs.v: ASTM C1153 requires every suspected wet area to be verified by core cut, probe, or calibrated moisture meter, because a thermal anomaly indicates suspected moisture rather than a diagnosis; a core cut confirms its presence, depth, and extent, per ASTM and Fluke, and the check matters most in winter, when the wet-area contrast narrows.
